title: "Figure 4—figure supplement (number pending) — the boundary-conditioned filter alone: how far its reported covariance is from the empirical one, interval by interval"
author: "Luciano Moffatt"

<!--
NUMBER PENDING, as for the other rebuilt supplements.

WHY A FIGURE FOR ONE MEMBER. The four-member ratio figure has to give each column its own vertical
scale, because least squares reaches a factor a hundred and the boundary-conditioned filter never
leaves 0.8 to 1.4. That buys visibility and costs comparability: heights cannot be read across
columns there. With IR alone the scale is SHARED by every panel, so a cell can be compared with any
other cell, which is the whole point of dedicating a figure to it. And the freed column axis goes
to the acquisition interval, all seven of them, instead of the three a shared figure can carry.

WHAT IS PLOTTED, and it is the ratio and not the quantile-quantile. For each fit, the squared
Mahalanobis distance from the cloud mean divided by the chi-squared quantile it should have sat at:

    d2_k / chi2_p(k/(n+1))

A calibrated covariance is a HORIZONTAL LINE AT ONE. A covariance wrong by a constant factor is a
horizontal line at that factor, read straight off the axis. A wrong SHAPE -- a distribution that is
not chi-squared however it is scaled -- is the only thing that tilts the line. The quantile-quantile
version of the same data spends the panel on a 45-degree line and hides departures of ten per cent;
here they are the whole picture. The sibling figures carry the conventional rendering for a reader
who expects it.

DASHED IS WHAT IR REPORTS, its Fisher covariance; SOLID is the distortion-corrected sandwich. Both
are the aggregate matrices from the battery at the same cell, divided by the group size because the
cloud is a group of a hundred recordings and the battery matrix is per recording.

THE GREY BAND IS THE NULL, simulated per panel at this panel's own n and six degrees of freedom.
It is WIDE here, and that is the honest consequence of a hundred fits per curve: the ratio of a
single order statistic to its expectation wanders a long way even when everything is right. A
curve inside the band has said nothing. Read the BODY of the distribution, on the left, where the
band is narrow and there are dozens of points behind every value; the right-hand end is four points
and belongs to the band.

WHAT THE FIGURE IS FOR. IR is the member the paper argues is calibrated, so this is where that
claim is most exposed. If its dashed curve sits on one across the plane, the claim holds without
the correction; where it does not, the correction has to carry it, and the solid curve says
whether it does.

POOLED OVER THE SIX NOISE LEVELS, and that is the difference between this figure saying something
and saying nothing. Its first version inherited the four-member figure's fixed noise of 0.1, which
was there because least squares has clouds at no other level; IR has SIX at every channel count,
0.05 to 10, so five sixths of its data were being left on disk. Pooling them is licit for the same
reason pooling the intervals is: d2 is chi-squared with six degrees of freedom whatever the cell,
so the reference does not move and the samples can be sorted together. It takes each panel from a
hundred fits to about six hundred and narrows the null band by a factor of two and a half, which is
what turns "inside the band" from a statement about the sample size into a statement about IR.

The cost is the usual one for pooling and the table at the foot guards it: if IR were calibrated at
low noise and not at high, the pooled curve would show their average and hide the difference. The
per-noise medians are printed so that cannot pass unnoticed.
-->

```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE, warning = FALSE, message = FALSE)
suppressMessages({ library(data.table); library(ggplot2) })
```

```{r data}
# This notebook does its OWN sweep rather than reading the four-member source data, because that
# one is built at a single noise level for a reason that does not apply here. Written as CSV with
# the same stamp discipline as everything else in the set.
SRC   <- "../figure_4_source_data/figure_4_source_data_qq_IR.csv"
A     <- "macro_IR"
# the small counts are in the sweep too: the second render is about them
NCHS  <- c(5, 10, 20, 50, 100, 1000, 10000)
NCH_MAIN  <- c(10, 100, 1000, 10000)   # the decade ladder, the first render
NCH_SMALL <- c(5, 10, 20, 50)          # the few-channel corner, the zoom
ZS    <- c("0.05", "0.1", "0.2", "0.5", "1", "10")
GS    <- 100
COV   <- c(reported = "Probit_statistics_Gaussian_Fisher_Covariance",
           sandwich = "Probit_statistics_Gaussian_Distortion_Corrected_Covariance")
.f <- function(n, z, kind)
  Sys.glob(file.path("../data", "*",
                     sprintf("figure_3_G_nch_%d_nsim_10000_%s_noise_%s_%s.csv", n, A, z, kind)))

stamp <- local({
  fs <- unlist(lapply(NCHS, function(n) unlist(lapply(ZS, function(z)
    c(.f(n, z, "mle_cloud_runs"), .f(n, z, "battery_pool_G"))))))
  i <- file.info(c(fs, "figure_4_supplement_qq_IR.Rmd"))
  sprintf("# figure_4 qq IR | files=%d bytes=%.0f newest=%.0f", length(fs),
          sum(i$size, na.rm = TRUE), max(as.numeric(i$mtime), na.rm = TRUE))
})

ir_cell <- function(n, z) {
  fc <- .f(n, z, "mle_cloud_runs"); fb <- .f(n, z, "battery_pool_G")
  if (!length(fc) || !length(fb)) return(NULL)
  d <- fread(fc[1], skip = 1, showProgress = FALSE)
  b <- fread(fb[1], skip = 1, showProgress = FALSE)
  rbindlist(lapply(sort(unique(d$interval_in_tau)), function(dlt) {
    cv <- d[variable == "Convergence_Status_Code" & group_size == GS & interval_in_tau == dlt]
    ok <- if (nrow(cv)) cv$sample_index[cv$value == 0] else NULL
    TH <- d[variable == "Model_Parameters_Hat" & group_size == GS & interval_in_tau == dlt &
            (is.null(ok) | sample_index %in% ok)]
    if (!nrow(TH)) return(NULL)
    W <- dcast(TH, sample_index ~ param_index, value.var = "value")
    M <- as.matrix(W[, -1]); if (nrow(M) < 20) return(NULL)
    pid <- as.integer(colnames(M)); P <- length(pid)
    C <- sweep(M, 2, colMeans(M), "-")
    rbindlist(lapply(names(COV), function(k) {
      g <- b[component_path == COV[[k]] & statistic == "value" & probit == "mean" &
             abs(interval_in_tau - dlt) < 1e-9 & param_index %in% pid & param_col %in% pid]
      if (!nrow(g)) { cat(sprintf("    SKIP N_ch %d noise %s Delta %g %s: no rows\n",
                                  n, z, dlt, k)); return(NULL) }
      S <- matrix(NA_real_, P, P)
      S[cbind(match(g$param_index, pid), match(g$param_col, pid))] <- g$value
      if (anyNA(S)) { cat(sprintf("    SKIP N_ch %d noise %s Delta %g %s: gaps\n",
                                  n, z, dlt, k)); return(NULL) }
      Si <- try(solve(S / GS), silent = TRUE)
      if (inherits(Si, "try-error")) { cat(sprintf("    SKIP N_ch %d noise %s Delta %g %s: singular\n",
                                                   n, z, dlt, k)); return(NULL) }
      data.table(nch = n, z = z, dlt = dlt, cov = k, p = P,
                 d2 = rowSums((C %*% Si) * C))
    }))
  }))
}

if (file.exists(SRC) && identical(readLines(SRC, n = 1), stamp)) {
  cat("qq IR: source CSV is current, reading it\n")
  D <- as.data.table(read.csv(SRC, skip = 1))
} else {
  cat("qq IR: sweeping IR's clouds over six noise levels\n")
  D <- rbindlist(lapply(NCHS, function(n) rbindlist(lapply(ZS, function(z) {
    r <- ir_cell(n, z)
    if (!is.null(r)) cat(sprintf("  N_ch %-6d noise %-5s  %d values\n", n, z, nrow(r)))
    r
  }))))
  dir.create(dirname(SRC), showWarnings = FALSE, recursive = TRUE)
  writeLines(stamp, SRC)
  suppressWarnings(write.table(D, SRC, sep = ",", row.names = FALSE, col.names = TRUE,
                               append = TRUE, qmethod = "double"))
}

# POOL over the noise levels: sort the combined sample per (N_ch, Delta, covariance) and give it
# the chi-squared quantiles of its own length.
QALL <- D[, .(emp = sort(d2), p = p[1]), by = .(nch, dlt, cov)]
QALL[, theo := qchisq(ppoints(.N), p[1]), by = .(nch, dlt, cov)]
DLTS <- sort(unique(QALL$dlt))
Q <- QALL[nch %in% NCH_MAIN]
NCHS <- NCH_MAIN
Q[, nchf := factor(sprintf("N[ch]==%d", nch), levels = sprintf("N[ch]==%d", NCHS))]
Q[, dltf := factor(sprintf("Delta==%g", dlt), levels = sprintf("Delta==%g", DLTS))]

set.seed(1)
BAND <- Q[cov == "sandwich", {
  n <- .N; M <- replicate(2000, sort(rchisq(n, p[1])))
  th <- qchisq(ppoints(n), p[1])
  .(theo = th, lo = apply(M, 1, quantile, .025) / th, hi = apply(M, 1, quantile, .975) / th)
}, by = .(nch, nchf, dlt, dltf)]
NF <- Q[cov == "sandwich", .(n = .N), by = .(nchf, dltf)]
cat(sprintf("IR: %d panels, %d to %d fits each (pooled over %d noise levels)\n",
            nrow(NF), min(NF$n), max(NF$n), length(ZS)))
```

```{r plot, fig.width = 7.0, fig.height = 4.6}
mk_band <- function(QQ) { set.seed(1); QQ[cov == "sandwich", {
  n <- .N; M <- replicate(2000, sort(rchisq(n, p[1]))); th <- qchisq(ppoints(n), p[1])
  .(theo = th, lo = apply(M, 1, quantile, .025) / th, hi = apply(M, 1, quantile, .975) / th)
}, by = .(nch, nchf, dlt, dltf)] }

g <- ggplot(Q[theo > 1], aes(theo, emp / theo, linetype = cov)) +
  geom_ribbon(data = BAND[theo > 1], aes(x = theo, ymin = lo, ymax = hi),
              inherit.aes = FALSE, fill = "grey85", colour = NA) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 1, colour = "#1A9850", linewidth = .35) +
  geom_line(linewidth = .4, colour = "#08306B") +
  facet_grid(nchf ~ dltf, labeller = label_parsed) +
  scale_x_log10(breaks = c(1, 5, 20)) +
  scale_y_log10(breaks = c(0.5, 1, 2, 4)) +
  coord_cartesian(ylim = c(0.35, 5)) +
  scale_linetype_manual(values = c(reported = "22", sandwich = "solid"), name = NULL) +
  labs(x = expression("theoretical quantile, " * chi[6]^2 * " (log)"),
       y = expression("empirical " * d^2 * " over theoretical (log)")) +
  theme_bw(base_size = 8, base_family = "Helvetica") +
  theme(panel.grid.minor = element_blank(), legend.position = "bottom",
        legend.key.size = unit(9, "pt"), strip.text = element_text(size = 7),
        axis.text = element_text(size = 6.5), axis.title = element_text(size = 8),
        legend.text = element_text(size = 7))
g
ggsave("Figure_4_supplement_qq_IR.pdf", g, width = 7.0, height = 4.6)
```

```{r small, fig.width = 7.0, fig.height = 4.6}
# THE FEW-CHANNEL CORNER, ZOOMED. Same quantity, same pooling, four rows of small channel counts
# and a vertical range of 0.75 to 1.35 instead of 0.35 to 5. This is where the paper expects the
# boundary-conditioned filter to degrade -- the occupancy closure is worst when the binomial has
# few channels to be normal about -- so it is where a departure of ten per cent is worth seeing,
# and on the full-range axis ten per cent is a line width.
#
# N_ch 5 HAS ONE NOISE LEVEL, not six, so its row pools about a hundred fits per panel against the
# six hundred of the rows below it, and its null band is correspondingly wider. The band is
# simulated per panel so it carries that difference itself; the row is not comparable to the others
# by eye without reading the band.
#
# CURVES ARE CLIPPED at the panel edge here, which the full-range render does not do. That is the
# price of the zoom and it is only paid in the extreme quantiles, where the band is wide and
# nothing can be concluded anyway.
QS <- QALL[nch %in% NCH_SMALL]
QS[, nchf := factor(sprintf("N[ch]==%d", nch), levels = sprintf("N[ch]==%d", NCH_SMALL))]
QS[, dltf := factor(sprintf("Delta==%g", dlt), levels = sprintf("Delta==%g", DLTS))]
BS <- mk_band(QS)
NS <- QS[cov == "sandwich", .(n = .N), by = .(nchf, dltf)]
cat(sprintf("IR small: %d panels, %d to %d fits each\n", nrow(NS), min(NS$n), max(NS$n)))

gs <- ggplot(QS[theo > 1], aes(theo, emp / theo, linetype = cov)) +
  geom_ribbon(data = BS[theo > 1], aes(x = theo, ymin = lo, ymax = hi),
              inherit.aes = FALSE, fill = "grey85", colour = NA) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 1, colour = "#1A9850", linewidth = .35) +
  geom_line(linewidth = .4, colour = "#08306B") +
  facet_grid(nchf ~ dltf, labeller = label_parsed) +
  scale_x_log10(breaks = c(1, 5, 20)) +
  scale_y_log10(breaks = c(0.8, 0.9, 1, 1.1, 1.25)) +
  coord_cartesian(ylim = c(0.75, 1.35)) +
  scale_linetype_manual(values = c(reported = "22", sandwich = "solid"), name = NULL) +
  labs(x = expression("theoretical quantile, " * chi[6]^2 * " (log)"),
       y = expression("empirical " * d^2 * " over theoretical (log)")) +
  theme_bw(base_size = 8, base_family = "Helvetica") +
  theme(panel.grid.minor = element_blank(), legend.position = "bottom",
        legend.key.size = unit(9, "pt"), strip.text = element_text(size = 7),
        axis.text = element_text(size = 6.5), axis.title = element_text(size = 8),
        legend.text = element_text(size = 7))
gs
ggsave("Figure_4_supplement_qq_IR_small.pdf", gs, width = 7.0, height = 4.6)

knitr::kable(dcast(QS[theo > 1 & theo < qchisq(0.90, 6),
                      .(ratio = median(emp / theo)), by = .(nch, dlt, cov)],
                   dlt ~ nch + cov, value.var = "ratio"), digits = 3,
             caption = "median d2/chi2 over the body, IR at few channels")
```

```{r numbers}
# the median ratio over the BODY of the distribution, where the band is narrow: one number per cell
body <- Q[theo > 1 & theo < qchisq(0.90, 6),
          .(ratio = median(emp / theo)), by = .(nch, dlt, cov)]
knitr::kable(dcast(body, dlt ~ nch + cov, value.var = "ratio"), digits = 3,
             caption = "median d2/chi2 over the body, IR, pooled over the six noise levels")

# THE GUARD ON THE POOLING: the same median resolved BY noise. If these disagree, the pooled curve
# is an average of unlike things and the figure has to be split.
pn <- D[, .(emp = sort(d2), p = p[1]), by = .(nch, z, cov)]
pn[, theo := qchisq(ppoints(.N), p[1]), by = .(nch, z, cov)]
knitr::kable(dcast(pn[theo > 1 & theo < qchisq(0.90, 6) & cov == "reported",
                      .(ratio = median(emp / theo)), by = .(nch, z)],
                   z ~ nch, value.var = "ratio"), digits = 3,
             caption = "the same, resolved by noise level (reported covariance): the pooling guard")
```
